focus: The smartphone receiver on the ground remaining completely passive while receiving incoming signals
output.how: Vertical composition with the satellite anchored at the upper third and the phone at the lower third. Connect satellite to phone, then trigger a downward flow animation. Use focus to frame the phone receiver and de-emphasize the space segment as the narration finishes.
output.rationale: Directly confronts the viewer with the core engineering paradox: if the device never sends a ping, how can it compute its exact position? Keeping visual noise low and isolating the one-way downlink makes the listening-only constraint unmistakable.
what: A satellite icon positioned at the top of the frame representing space
A smartphone rectangle icon positioned at the bottom representing the ground receiver
A directional connection line between the satellite and phone
A downward signal pulse flowing from satellite to phone
A status text badge indicating passive receive-only mode
output.when: The satellite and phone are shown at the start. As narration begins ('Your phone never transmits...'), a connection forms and signals flow downward from the satellite. The camera then focuses tightly on the phone to highlight the absence of any outgoing signals.
output.why: Establishes the fundamental asymmetry of GPS: satellites transmit signals down to Earth, while the user receiver remains entirely silent with no uplink.
